intended_object: The Chevalley ℤ-form (Chevalley order) of a split semisimple Lie algebra L over a field of characteristic zero, attached to a Chevalley system (x_α) (Bourbaki, Lie VIII §2.4 and §12; Humphreys §25.2). It is the ℤ-span of the root vectors x_α and the coroots H_α, viewed as a ℤ-Lie subalgebra of L. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the names.
explanation:
The definition is `rootCorootLieSubalgebra`, applied with the integrality of the structure constants that a Chevalley system provides. It is a `LieSubalgebra ℤ L` whose carrier is `rootCorootSpan x`, the ℤ-span of {x α} ∪ {coroot α}.

Under `IsChevalleySystem`, `IsSl2System` gives three things: x α lies in the root space of α; [x α, x (−α)] = coroot α; and x α = 0 at the zero weight. So the zero weight contributes only 0 to the span and adds nothing spurious. The automorphism ω satisfies ω(x_α) = −x_{−α}, which is Bourbaki's definition of a Chevalley system.

The span uses the coroots of all roots rather than only the simple ones. This gives the same lattice, because the coroots form a root system and every coroot is an integer combination of the simple coroots. The result is therefore exactly the ℤ-span of a Chevalley basis, which is the standard Chevalley lattice. Closure under the bracket is the theorem `exists_int_lie_eq_smul`, which is supplied as the proof argument; it is not an extra assumption.

The setting is the natural one for this notion: a field of characteristic zero, a nondegenerate Killing form (i.e. semisimple), finite dimension, and a splitting Cartan subalgebra. Mathlib has no Chevalley ℤ-form.
